name: textreclaim
description: A DRY POOL TAKES BANKS BACK FROM UNUSED TEXTS: twenty-five distinct programs run once and exit, leaving their texts cached (2.11BSD keeps all text sticky in an LRU cache), and then twenty sleeps are spawned (twenty: the script's shell is one more of the 32 processes).  Bank_Alloc, finding the pool dry, frees the least recently used text no process runs (xuncore) before it asks the Memory Manager.  Every sleep must start: `too big' (sh's word for ENOMEM from exec) is asserted absent, and the marker is built by expansion so the typed line cannot satisfy it.  textchurn_check.py then holds the references balanced and every bank to one owner after the reclaims.
